summary: The cardholder starts with no balance, makes purchases that push the account above its credit limit, and reaches statement close while still over limit. The scenario is designed to test over-limit behavior at statement close while also including bound events for the modeled credit-limit, grace-period, and minimum-payment obligations.
assumptions: The account has no previous balance at the start of this billing cycle, so the purchase grace-period concept is in scope under the contract.

The issuer permits the purchases to post even though the resulting outstanding balance exceeds the credit limit; the contract makes the cardholder liable for credit extended in excess of the limit and contemplates over-limit status on a statement date.

The over-limit fee described in the markdown is not separately modeled in the allowed clause-id list for obligation-binding, so this scenario focuses on the over-limit condition existing at statement close rather than modeling the fee itself as a performed obligation.
Because the archetype centers on statement-close over-limit behavior, the minimum-payment obligation is included via a later due-date payment event after statement close.

The grace-period obligation is represented by a notice event at statement close indicating that at least 25 days remain before purchase interest would be imposed, consistent with there being no previous balance.
